pr_title: DNN: Make MatMul layer support 3D or 4D operation with const input
pr_body:
**Merge with extra:** https://github.com/opencv/opencv_extra/pull/1015

This PR is a temporary solution to fix #22713.

When 3D or 4D `MatMul` with a const input, it will create a virtual layer to ensure it can be run correctly. Later I will create a new PR to optimize the parsing of `MatMul` so that 3D or 4D operations can also use SIMD and multi-thread acceleration like 2D `MatMul`.

      Patch to opencv_extra has the same branch name.

issue_context.title: BUG ONNXImporter::handleNode MatMul
issue_context.body:
### System Information

OpenCV version: current Master branch 
Operating System / Platform: Windows 11
Compiler & compiler version: MSVC 16


### Detailed description

When trying to parse the onnx file (exported from https://github.com/baudm/parseq and simplified with https://github.com/daquexian/onnx-simplifier as recommended in the opencv doku) i get following error:

> ERROR:0@0.145] global X:\ThirdPartySource\opencv_cuda\opencv\modules\dnn\src\onnx\onnx_importer.cpp (1050) cv::dnn::dnn4_v20220524::ONNXImporter::handleNode DNN/ONNX: ERROR during processing node with 2 inputs and 1 outputs: [MatMul]:(onnx_node!MatMul_859) from domain='ai.onnx'
OpenCV: terminate handler is called! The last OpenCV error is:
OpenCV(4.6.0-dev) Error: Unspecified error (> Node [MatMul@ai.onnx]:(onnx_node!MatMul_859) parse error: OpenCV(4.6.0-dev) X:\ThirdPartySource\opencv_cuda\opencv\modules\core\src\matrix_transform.cpp:245: error: (-215:Assertion failed) _src.dims() <= 2 && esz <= 32 in function 'cv::transpose'
> ) in cv::dnn::dnn4_v20220524::ONNXImporter::handleNode, file X:\ThirdPartySource\opencv_cuda\opencv\modules\dnn\src\onnx\onnx_importer.cpp, line 1069

The onnx it self is valid and can be used with the onnx runtime itself.
i also checked it via https://netron.app/

there seems to be 2 issues in MatMul_859 first i think opencv expect another order of the inputs.
But even if i change them i get another error here i am :)



### Steps to reproduce

auto detector = cv::dnn::readNetFromONNX("ocr-sim.onnx");


weetransfer for the onnx file:

https://wetransfer.com/downloads/46d0dc6287c0d1ed000924a036400bbe20221028095359/f7770d3acc028f8006a96bced82790c920221028095418/e4e0a6



### Issue submission checklist

- [X] I report the issue, it's not a question
- [X] I checked the problem with documentation, FAQ, open issues, forum.opencv.org, Stack Overflow, etc and have not found any solution
- [X] I updated to the latest OpenCV version and the issue is still there
- [X] There is reproducer code and related data files (videos, images, onnx, etc)

@Compaile Thanks for your reproduce model, I will check the details.

Hi @Compaile, thanks for your report. 

The reason is that `MatMul` is only support 2D mat, can not support 3D or 4D mat. I'm working on it right now.

@Compaile Hi, thanks for your report. Please look at your model first.

The node `MatMul_859` has wrong input. `MatMul` operator is used as `A x B` when shape A is `12x26x32` and shape B is `12x32x128`. The output shape should be `12x26x128`. However, your model seems to use `MatMul` as `B x A`, it's obvioursly not allowed.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49567307/199903109-04153d23-5ca0-480e-90b1-69d095548c35.png)

Even loading this model by `onnxruntime` doesn't parse it correctly.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49567307/199900218-2d5b8031-7bfb-4a28-a8f4-e44bfb9ca72d.png)

In addition, OpenCV does support 3D or 4D MatMul. But there still some bugs when parse the node like that in your model. So I will try to fix it.

review_comments: const reference in signature and copy call on the first line looks very strange. I propose to pass `node_proto` as value, or, better, make a copy in else branch only to not degrade existing branch performance.
Agree, this `const reference` exists in many onnx op codes.
Then the second option is the best one: "better, make a copy in else branch only to not degrade existing branch performance"

@asmorkalov Some handlers in original code tries to hijack passed protobuf nodes - this is a bug (legacy design bug then we have large `if/else if` code instead of dedicated handlers - see #20478).

Handlers are not intended to modify protobuf nodes (nobody expects/needs that), so `const reference` is correct.
